experiment: Which law shapes can a derived generator actually refute?
design: Every stub in fixtures/verify-refutability is deliberately WRONG. Therefore any measured-bothPass is a FALSE NEGATIVE of the verifier, not a debatable result. No judgement call is needed to read the outcome.
hypothesis: CLAUDE.md: a property whose failure needs two generated values to COLLIDE is invisible to a generator drawing from a realistic domain. So: BROAD refuted, COLLISION survives, EDGE refuted iff the edge pass earns its keep.

scoring.REFUTED: verify reports defaultFails (or edgeCaseAdvisory naming the violation)

subtraction; fails for every a != b
decode drops a character; fails for every non-empty
tie-break only observable when two timestamps are EQUAL; the Decisions.merge shape, already measured as bothPass at 100 trials
needs two generated values in the same bucket (value % 8)
needs two generated intervals to be exactly adjacent
wrong only at Int.max; the verifier runs a dedicated edge pass and Int.max is the canonical integer edge

result.coverage_rate: 6/44 = 14% of proposed laws produced ANY verdict

scored_predictions.note: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED on a purpose-built case: wrong only at multiples of 997, never drawn.
PREDICTION WRONG, and the reason is worse than the miss: the edge pass reported ZERO trials, so Int.min was never tried.

unpredicted.note: my union is BROADLY non-commutative (asymmetric drop), so this is a BROAD row, consistent with BROAD->refuted.

result.conclusion: Verification cannot substitute for precision TODAY, and the binding constraint is REACH rather than generator quality. 86% of proposed laws were never measured. Of the 14% that ran: the collision-dependent violation passed 100 trials while being false, and the edge-dependent one passed with the edge pass reporting zero trials.

edge_bias_experiment_2026_07_31.question: The EDGE-class prediction (REFUTED) was scored WRONG because verify returned bothPass with edgeTrials=0. Was that a generator-tuning problem or a verifier defect?
edge_bias_experiment_2026_07_31.what_was_found: A verifier defect. `edgeSentinelSection()` emits a hardcoded `print("VERIFY_EDGE_RESULT: PASS")` with zero trials for EVERY strategist-routed carrier, justified as 'integral or String — no NaN/Inf semantic, no edge pass needed'. That conflates floating-point edge cases with edge cases. Separately, `Gen<Int>.int()` spans `.min ... .max`, so Int.min is drawn with probability ~2^-58 over 100 trials.
edge_bias_experiment_2026_07_31.what_was_tried: Mix the curated boundary values (min/max/0/-1/1) into the DEFAULT generator at 3:2 weight, mirroring what V1.150 already does for String.

it_worked_on_the_target.mergedBound(_:) commutativity: measured-bothPass -> measured-defaultFails at trial 6, shrunk to (0, Int.min)
it_worked_on_the_target.surviving bothPass in 44: 1 — canonicalizedOffset(), the COLLISION stub, which this fix correctly does not target
it_worked_on_the_target.hypothesis_status: BROAD refuted / EDGE refuted / COLLISION survives — complete

AND IT WAS REVERTED.why: It breaks integer verification generally. `x + 1` traps at Int.max; at uniform draw that is ~100/2^64 and effectively never, at 40% weight it is certain. Three VerifyPipelineLifted integration tests went from bothPass to `measured-error: the verifier trapped (signal 5)`.
AND IT WAS REVERTED.the_dependency_is_documented: Tests/SwiftInferIntegrationTests/VerifyPipelineLiftedIntegrationTests.swift:86-92 states it outright: '`x + 1` overflow-traps only at `x == Int.max` — probability ~100/2^64 over 100 trials, effectively zero. Operations like `x * 2` would overflow ~50% of trials and crash.' Integer verification RESTS on boundary values being unreachable.
AND IT WAS REVERTED.my_wrong_claim: The reverted docstring argued the change 'changes the frequency, not the possibility'. True literally, wrong practically — frequency is the whole mechanism the existing design depends on.

edge_bias_experiment_2026_07_31.the_correct_design: Boundary values belong in a SEPARATE pass whose failure is advisory, not a verdict — the mechanism `VerifyOutcome.edgeCaseAdvisory` already provides, and which the FP path already uses for NaN/Infinity for exactly this reason (NaN breaks real laws too). A trap in an advisory pass does not invalidate the default-pass verdict. Cost: each template composer emits its law body once, so a real second pass means emitting it twice.
edge_bias_experiment_2026_07_31.what_shipped_instead: Only the renderer fix. `edgeTrials == 0` now says the edge pass did not run, instead of '(integer carrier — edge pass not applicable)', which read as 'this carrier has no edge cases'.
